title.narrative: Lifesaving Winterization Response to the Most Vulnerable People in Northwest Syria

description.narrative: TAS through this project will address the vital winterization requirements of the most vulnerable individuals and adapt to shocks anticipated in the winter season 2022 / 2023, such as significant snowfall, flooding, and unexpected population shifts brought on by the resumption of hostilities, in so, this winterization approach will boost the thermal comfort of homes (HHs) during the winter months. The project will target Dana (Alkaramah Camp Clusters) and Salqin communities, with a total of 11500 HHs mainly IDPs and part of the HCs(12,420 Men, 15,180 Women, 19,320 Boys, 22,080 Girls). The distribution will be through the Cash and Voucher Support (CVA) in response to winterization and emergency lifesaving needs through Multipurpose cash assistance (MPCA/CASH for wither) where each HH will receive $150 as a one-off distribution by the following activities: - TAS will visit targeted camps and conduct a meeting with the local actors and IDPs representatives (males and females)in order to explain the project and its goals and take any suggestions which help in the success of the project. - TAS has previously registered the project's beneficiaries by providing them food assistance on a monthly basis this project will focus on new and long-term IDPs who did not receive winter assistance. The most vulnerable IDPs who reside in the targeted area and match the selection criteria will therefore be the project's primary emphasis, with particular attention paid to women, children-headed households, disabled people, sick, PLW, and the elderly. - TAS has a long-term contract with an e-voucher service provider in Turkey, to provide the e-voucher system and its devices on the other hand, TAS has a long-term contract with several Financial Services Providers (FSPs) to provide mobile redemption points to exchange beneficiaries’ vouchers with money in Syria. - Once the beneficiary list has been imported into the E-voucher system database, TAS team will design, customize, and generate the QR codes with all the needed additional information and attributes. TAS will ask the E-voucher provider to provide 11,500 one-time E-vouchers to be distributed in the targeted locations to the targeted families, these vouchers can be redeemed through a mobile application that designed by the E-voucher Service Provider. The selected beneficiary will present at the distribution point to receive the voucher, and he/she will be informed by our team of the exact time of the redemption, then the beneficiary goes with the voucher and personal ID to the FSP point, and our team is there to read the voucher through a mobile application for the voucher provider when reading the QR appears on the mobile the beneficiary’s data, TAS team will matches the data of the beneficiary with the ID, and if it matches, it gives me a sign to the financial service provider to hand the money to the beneficiary. The FSP collects the vouchers and delivers them to the TAS financial department and receives his money after verifying all vouchers + the commission rate. - After distributing the MPCA/CASH for wither to the post-conflict-affected families, TAS team will collect the required documents and reports about the MPCA redemption, the redeemed vouchers will be paid to FSP within 15 working days after finalizing the redemption process and collecting the required data. - We will conduct a PDM to ensure that the service arrived to the beneficiaries smoothly and to measure beneficiaries' satisfactory - Principles of Do No Harm will be applied in all activities through several visits to monitor the distribution - We will coordinate with NGOs and the clusters to avoid any potential overlap and duplications.
